zh-CN.Spatial apps need clear reasons to leave: Spatial apps need clear reasons to leave the flat screen. The strongest use cases involve scale, hands-free context, spatial memory, or 3D inspection.
zh-CN.The practical reason this topic is getti: The practical reason this topic is getting attention in 2026 is simple: spatial devices keep improving while teams search for practical non-demo use cases. For product teams considering headsets, 3D interfaces, and mixed-reality workflows, the question is no longer whether the trend is interesting. The question is where it changes daily work enough to justify new process, budget, or risk review.
zh-CN.The common failure mode is turning a nor: The common failure mode is turning a normal dashboard into floating panels without improving the task. That mistake usually happens when a trend is treated as a feature checklist instead of an operating change. The technology may be new, but the weak point is often ownership, permissions, data quality, recovery, or review.
zh-CN.Before picking a vendor or writing code,: Before picking a vendor or writing code, decide what the user gains from depth, room awareness, gestures, or hands-free operation. A clear first decision keeps the team from mixing experiments, production systems, sensitive data, and customer promises into one blurry rollout.
zh-CN.Start small: prototype only the interact: Start small: prototype only the interaction that truly benefits from space and test fatigue early. Keep the first version narrow enough that success and failure are both visible. That makes it easier to compare quality, cost, latency, privacy, and support load before expanding the workflow.
zh-CN.A mature workflow produces a spatial pro: A mature workflow produces a spatial product brief that names the 3D advantage and the fallback screen workflow. It should be easy for someone outside the implementation team to inspect what happened, understand why it happened, and decide whether the result is reliable enough to act on.
zh-CN.Set a review date, a measurable success: Set a review date, a measurable success criterion, and a rollback path before launch. If the spatial computing workflow does not improve the actual decision, reduce risk, save time, or create a clearer user experience, keep it in research instead of forcing it into production.
